scope: Search saved user messages and reply bodies across accessible tasks, alongside existing header matches. Return bounded original-text snippets and exact turn/role links; preserve pagination, filters, drafts, history and scope. Global all-results navigation clears an inherited favorites filter.
prior_behavior: Application.runs searched only initial goals, display names, IDs, scenarios and agent names. An isolated existing three-turn task returned zero matches for both its third user message and saved reply text.

coverage: Followup and reply-only matches map to the root and exact turn
One task per result and filtering before pagination
Existing header matches avoid body reads
Literal symbols and Unicode lowercase expansion

iterations.note: The new verifier accessed runHistory before initial page loading created it; its readiness condition now requires the object to exist. The three existing regression suites passed in the same run.
The verifier tried to find an exact standalone text node for a command option whose accessible name also includes help text. It now locates the actual option by role/name.

Functional assertions passed, but visual review found multiline context hiding the matched phrase in an inner scroll region. The excerpt now wraps normally without a height clamp; width is bounded to preserve neighboring table columns. Final browser assertions also require the actual mark to be visible.

browser.visual_review: Inspected final light/dark task results, highlighted literal search phrase, role/round label, neighboring status and execution columns, keyboard focus and naturally wrapped snippets. Eight final layout cases verify real 28px text, viewport bounds, no horizontal excerpt overflow and visible matched text.
browser.isolation: 105 temporary synthetic tasks with Mock runtime snapshots. Tests traverse all 104 active matches across three pages, include the archived match via global search, verify favorite filtering, edit one held queue message, restore a draft and history, reload a role/turn deep link, delay a real HTTP response and switch workspace. Search/navigation requests are read-only; the single POST is the explicitly tested synthetic queued-message edit.

measurement.note: 80 tasks, 320 turns, 32768-byte reply padding per turn and audit padding per event. Four measured queries took 0.0789–0.1439 seconds; 50 saved-reply hits returned 57376 bytes. Single-machine observations, not a production capacity guarantee.

limits: Cross-task body search covers saved current user messages and report content, answer or section bodies. In-progress previews, audit/process text, source citation details, configuration and old edit versions are excluded.
Header matches retain precedence. Each body-only matching task exposes its earliest matching message, not a count of every occurrence.

Literal source-text matching is not semantic retrieval or Markdown rendering. A visible phrase crossing markup may not match; navigation still locates the round if a stored-source match is not found by the in-dialog visible-text highlighter.

Body reads are on demand, batched in one snapshot, with no new persistent index. Catalog headers and body projection retain their existing separate read phases; no whole-catalog cross-request snapshot guarantee is added.
The workbench recent-task filter remains local to summaries. Full body search is in the task list and global search.
The deep link stores task, turn and role but not the private search query. Reload restores the message position, not the previous highlight query.
Desktop visual coverage is 1024/1440 widths with normal and enlarged snippet/input text, not all-device or uniform page zoom coverage.
Full and focused test counts overlap. Version remains 1.3.0; no publication or repeated fresh installation.
